strings.name: Diebedo Francis Kere
strings.role: Architect · Local materials, climate and community
strings.summary: Born in Gando, Burkina Faso, Kéré studied carpentry and architecture in Germany, combining professional training with his home region’s materials, climate and collaborative traditions. Community-built Gando Primary School uses clay bricks, a raised roof and ventilation to improve learning conditions. His practice expanded to schools, cultural facilities and temporary pavilions. The 2017 Serpentine Pavilion brought the experience of gathering beneath a tree to London; in 2022 he became the first African architect to win the Pritzker Prize.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1965–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Combined local materials, climate-responsive design and community participation in works including the Gando school, advancing African architecture and sustainable public construction.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birth and citizenship
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Born in Gando, Burkina Faso; holds Burkinabé and German citizenship
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Trained in carpentry in Germany; graduated in architecture from Technische Universität Berlin in 2004
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: A community builds its school
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Gando Primary School combines residents’ labor and knowledge with modern engineering, using local materials for a hot climate while supporting skills and educational opportunities.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Climate shapes public buildings
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: From Gando to Dakar, shade, ventilation, local brick and trees organize spaces that connect cultural and educational facilities with local life.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Goethe-Institut Dakar opens
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Local brick, ventilated walls and a tree-centered courtyard organize the cultural venue; at its inauguration he discussed material choices and reducing buildings’ energy use.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Receives the Pritzker Architecture Prize
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The first African architect to receive the prize, he was recognized for combining architectural quality, local resources and community needs.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Serpentine Pavilion opens in London
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Inspired by memories of gathering beneath a tree, blue walls and an open canopy create a place for shelter, conversation and rainwater collection.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Establishes Kéré Architecture in Berlin
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The success of Gando Primary School led to an independent practice, extending its experience into health, cultural and other public buildings.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Graduates and receives the Aga Khan Award
strings.timeline.event-05.text: He graduated from Technische Universität Berlin; Gando Primary School received the Aga Khan Award that year, drawing international attention to its participatory and climatic approach.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Gando Primary School is completed
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Residents helped build his first school project in his home village, using clay-cement bricks, a raised roof and ventilation to improve classrooms in a hot climate.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Founds a fundraising organization for Gando
strings.timeline.event-07.text: He established the organization later renamed the Kéré Foundation to raise funds for the village school and advocate for comfortable learning spaces for children.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Begins architectural study in Berlin
strings.timeline.event-08.text: A scholarship enabled him to enter Technische Universität Berlin after carpentry training and evening classes, while considering ways to improve schools at home.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Travels to Germany for carpentry training
strings.timeline.event-09.text: A vocational scholarship brought him to Berlin, where he learned to make roofs and furniture by day and attended secondary classes at night.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Gando
strings.timeline.event-10.text: He grew up in Gando, Burkina Faso, and left home for schooling because the village lacked a school; experiences in hot classrooms later motivated his work on better learning environments.
